source_crosschecks.finding: ToolExecutor.execute(tool_name, tool_input, skip_approval) has no approval_id/request_digest parameter. Approval polling is keyed by approval_id, but successful approval is later represented only by caller-set skip_approval=True at execution.

AgentLoop passes the same in-memory tool_call action/input after approval, which reduces accidental mismatch in this caller, but both safe and approved-risky paths call execute(..., skip_approval=True); the executor boundary does not mechanically consume a typed approval decision.

semantic_atoms.claim: Historical Project-Frankenstein contained genuine pre-execution human denial in the normal AgentLoop path, but approval identity was a workflow/UI correlation key rather than an executor-consumed capability bound to exact request bytes, generation and invocation identity.
preserve: risk-sensitive fast path versus approval path
do_not_preserve: caller-controlled skip_approval as the final authorization boundary
approval queue persistence of unrestricted full tool_input
tool-name-only safety classification as sufficient effect policy

architecture_deltas.delta: A Frankenstein-2.0 EffectDecision must be consumed at the actual executor boundary. It binds immutable invocation_id/tool_use_id + request_digest + generation + causal_id + policy version + expiry/one-shot state. The executor rejects missing, stale, mismatched or already-consumed decisions before a state-changing effect.

Human approval remains a useful decision input and UI workflow, but approval_id itself is not canonical effect authority. Approval must produce or update the typed EffectDecision that the executor consumes; UI approval storage must be redacted/digest-bound and cannot bypass deterministic policy.

Fuse complementary lineages rather than choosing one: historical AgentLoop contributes real pre-execution deny semantics; current stern.py contributes generation/idempotency bookkeeping and post-execution outcome evidence. Frankenstein-2.0 must combine both behind one typed EffectGate/EffectJournal authority with immutable per-invocation binding.

contradictions.claim_a: Historical AgentLoop can stop a risky action before execute when approval is denied.
contradictions.claim_b: After approval, executor invocation does not consume approval_id or a digest-bound decision and relies on caller skip_approval=True.
contradictions.resolution: Preserve the pre-execution human-deny concept but replace the binding mechanism with executor-consumed typed EffectDecision. Production/runtime reachability of the historical path remains unpromoted.

hypotheses: The missing wache-koenig lineage may contain the transition from historical caller-side approval enforcement to later hook-side bookkeeping; recovering it could reveal reusable checks or explain why blocking was separated from stern.py.
Exact decision consumption at the executor boundary will make both human approval and automatic policy auditable without allowing either UI state or model output to become a second effect authority.
counterhypotheses: A historical wrapper may have revalidated approval contents before ToolExecutor.execute(); no such binding is established in the inspected executor/loop source.
If historical runtime had only one trusted AgentLoop caller, caller discipline may have made mismatches rare, but that does not satisfy the successor's explicit causal/effect authority contract.
next_exact_gate: Recover wache-koenig and any historical approval responder/wrapper that could revalidate or consume approvals, then require Triggerword-4 executor tests proving decision one-shot consumption, request-digest mismatch rejection, stale-generation rejection, deny non-execution and exact result re-entry.
